summary: The shared solver-owned foam surface now uses scene lighting and two independently advected, incommensurate samples of each river's first-party lace instead of one static unlit rectangular tile. Matched cold-water evidence materially reduces continuous bright rails, but retained strokes, analytical wave geometry, incomplete aerated volume and spray, synthetic environments, and absent external acceptance keep the milestone fail-closed.

implementation.solver_mask: vertex alpha remains the first multiplier before lace breakup
implementation.raft_exclusion: the runtime-updated raft ellipse remains the final opacity-mask multiplier

futaleufu_breaking_water_side.visual_verdict: Retain. The dense rectangular white lattice becomes smaller disconnected patches and participates in direct light. Parallel analytical strokes and the smooth base wave remain visibly synthetic.

chilko_bank_closeup.visual_verdict: Retain as descriptive evidence only. Bright rails are less continuous and foam responds to scene light, but the matched frame also contains a different deterministic lace phase and a materially different direct-light distribution, so the luminance delta is not treated as an acceptance threshold.

validation.unreal_editor_build: SmokeEmIfYouGotEmEditor Mac Development succeeded after the final material and native-test changes
validation.native_material_audit: RaftSim.M9.FSharedFlowAdvectedFoam passed 1/1 with zero warnings and zero errors
validation.shared_water_and_runnable_maps: RaftSim.P2.WaterSurfaceRenders plus all six RaftSim.P4.RiverMapLoads passed 7/7; warnings were the engine motion-vector flag, established Troublemaker capsize telemetry, and the established Zambezi connectivity timeout
validation.matched_renderer_captures: Futaleufu breaking-water-side and Chilko bank-closeup captures completed at 1280x720 with the same commands and camera contracts as the baseline

remaining_photoreal_defects: The source lace itself still contains elongated high-contrast strokes, so some parallel line character remains after multiscale breakup.
The foam is a thin masked surface over low-resolution analytical wave geometry rather than a thick entrained-air body with resolved overturning crests, holes, pile, and recirculation.
Spray, suspended droplets, mist, rock-contact plumes, raft wake, paddle interaction, wet fabric, and camera-lens water remain incomplete or unapproved.

Terrain, banks, boulders, vegetation, atmosphere, raft equipment, characters, anatomy, PPE, animation, and hand/paddle contact remain below the requested photoreal target in at least one runnable river.
No named guide, geospatial, hydraulic, environment-art, water-VFX, rights, hazard-readability, product, or target-platform reviewer has approved full-scene promotion.
required_external_acceptance_gates: A named whitewater water-VFX and environment-art reviewer must approve the foam, crest, hole, spray, mist, reflection, transmission, and shoreline-contact presentation across representative flow bands.
Qualified guides for the represented rivers must approve rapid identity, aeration placement, line and hazard readability, and raft/swimmer occlusion at the represented flows.
A geospatial or technical-art reviewer must approve source alignment and the labeled procedural terrain, bank, bathymetry, and rapid-geometry infill boundaries.
A rights and provenance reviewer must approve every production texture, mesh, reference-media use, attribution, and redistribution record.
A safety and gameplay-readability reviewer must approve that foam, spray, mist, vegetation, lighting, raft, and characters do not hide hazards, swimmers, rescue targets, or solver failures.
Target-platform qualification must pass desktop performance, memory, streaming, fresh-machine rendering, and required VR or low-power readability budgets.
The product owner must approve the integrated moving-camera river, raft, equipment, character, animation, and water interaction presentation before M9 or photoreal promotion.
